overrides.canonStatus: Modern corpus name for funerary formulae inscribed in late Old Kingdom royal pyramids; later reuse varied by period and setting.
overrides.dateConfidence: Approximate late Old Kingdom range; UCL Digital Egypt identifies the pyramid of Unas as the earliest example and requires monument-level dating.
overrides.author: Anonymous ritual compositions; no single authorship asserted
overrides.description: A corpus of funerary formulae first preserved in the inner chambers of late Old Kingdom pyramids. The corpus is not one book or a complete account of Egyptian religion.
overrides.historicalContext: UCL Digital Egypt distinguishes the late Old Kingdom pyramid inscriptions from their later ritual and funerary reuse. Individual formulae and monuments require separate dating and witness records.
overrides.manuscripts: Inscribed pyramid chambers, beginning with Unas and continuing in pyramids of later kings and queens; UCL also documents later copies on other funerary surfaces.
overrides.sourceStatus: Reviewed academic metadata; no translation bundled
overrides.copyright: Metadata link only; translation rights not assessed

overrides.category: Funerary corpus / coffin and burial-chamber inscriptions
overrides.canonStatus: Modern corpus name for diverse Middle Kingdom funerary compositions; not a single fixed book.
overrides.dateConfidence: Approximate Middle Kingdom range stated by UCL Digital Egypt; individual witnesses require separate dating.
overrides.author: Anonymous funerary compositions; no single authorship asserted
overrides.description: Funerary compositions preserved especially on the interiors of Middle Kingdom coffins and burial chambers. The corpus draws partly on Pyramid Text traditions and includes material later found in Book of the Dead traditions.
overrides.historicalContext: The corpus label groups many compositions and witnesses. Continuity with earlier and later funerary corpora does not make the collections identical.
overrides.manuscripts: UCL Digital Egypt identifies decorated coffins and burial chambers, including material from Beni Hasan, Harageh and Sedment.
overrides.sourceStatus: Reviewed academic metadata; no translation bundled
overrides.copyright: Metadata link only; translation rights not assessed

records.title: Tale of Sinuhe

records.description: A Middle Egyptian narrative commonly known as the Tale of Sinuhe. The Atlas separates the composition from its surviving manuscripts and from later interpretation.
records.historicalContext: UCL Digital Egypt catalogs the work within Middle Kingdom literature and provides manuscript, transcription and translation research materials.

records.title: Westcar Papyrus Tales
records.canonStatus: Ancient Egyptian narrative compositions preserved together in a manuscript; not treated as a universal canon.
records.dateConfidence: UCL Digital Egypt includes the Westcar narratives in its Middle Egyptian literature survey; composition and manuscript dates require separate review.
records.author: Anonymous; narrative setting is not evidence of authorship or composition date
records.description: A group of ancient Egyptian narratives preserved on the manuscript conventionally called the Westcar Papyrus. Work, manuscript and narrated royal setting remain distinct records.
records.historicalContext: The cited UCL academic survey places the narratives within Middle Egyptian literary study. A dedicated manuscript record and reviewed bibliography remain outstanding.
records.manuscripts: Known through the Westcar Papyrus; repository identifiers and codicological details require a sourced witness record.
